content:
Apple today unveiled its latest Mac mini and Mac Studio models, and alongside the new machines, the company has also rolled out small updates to several of its Magic Keyboard accessories.

The latest Magic Keyboard drops the text labels on keycaps in favour of icons.

Apple's Mac mini and Mac Studio have been upgraded to the next-generation M6 chip and the high-end M5 Ultra, among other new chips, delivering a significant boost in performance.

The latest models are available to order now: order the Mac mini here, and the Mac Studio here.

Beyond the desktop changes, Apple has also refreshed its Magic Keyboard lineup, with the new models featuring one subtle tweak.

The latest Magic Keyboard removes the text labels from a number of keys, replacing them with icons instead.

Apple had already made the same change earlier on the MacBook Neo, MacBook Air and MacBook Pro, and the Magic Keyboard now adopts the same revision.

Here are the new Magic Keyboard models affected:

  • Magic Keyboard: US$99
  • Magic Keyboard with Touch ID: US$149
  • Magic Keyboard with Touch ID and Numeric Keypad: US$179

Commonly used keys such as Tab, Caps Lock, Return, Shift and Delete have all abandoned their text markings in favour of icons only. On the larger model with a numeric keypad, keys such as Home, Page Up and Page Down now use brand-new icons to replace the previous text.

From a top comment by Caesarrr

I really don't understand this change — it will definitely add friction for users, so what benefit is worth sacrificing UX?

Apart from the switch to icons, the new Magic Keyboard looks almost identical to the previous generation in every other respect, with full USB-C support and the same features and layout as before.

If you'd like to order the new Magic Keyboard through Amazon rather than Apple, you can do so here: Magic Keyboard, Touch ID version, Touch ID and Numeric Keypad version (black).

What do you think of the move to drop the text labels on the keys? Feel free to share your thoughts in the comments.
